TheVARGuy: Do We Need a More Open, Private, "Decentralized" Internet?

He seems to lack any understanding of what a decentralized internet would offer in terms of basic user access. Setup a site today? Make a page, buy a domain, buy a server, publish, and hope you don't offend anybody as the entire setup can be destroyed by any one of a very large number of people with control over "your" content.

Decentralized internet? Make a page. Click publish. Done. It's like the difference between "opening a bitcoin account" and opening a bank account. One you click a button - the other you turn over your life, hope they accept you, and then jump through a million hoops they impose on you. Even for sites whose model relies on centralization, like Voat, it would have a huge impact. Right now Voat's future is shaky for many reasons but the most obvious being money. More users - more bandwidth - more money. Decentralization means no individual entity is taking a disproportionate burden of the bandwidth.

This article was more about refined mudslinging than an actual consideration of the issue it was supposedly addressing. Even his argument for privacy was incredibly flimsy. Expecting users to be of upper to expert competency in terms of things like privacy methods is obviously completely and utterly unrealistic. Changing user behavior is a herculean task. Changing systems is, by comparison, trivial.
